condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

With the outbreak of COVID-19, resources were reprogrammed with the following targets: 4.1: Number of developed gender sensitive Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for maintaining law enforcement during COVID-19 by Zambia Police Service (ZPS) Baseline: 0, Target: 1 4.2: Number of police officers trained as master trainers on COVID-19 response by Zambia Police Baseline: 0, Target: 30 including 15 women officers 4.3: Number of police officers provided with actionable information on maintaining international human rights standards and preventing COVID-19 Baseline: 0, Target: 2,100 including at least 50% of women 4.4: Number of of information products distributed to police officers on Law enforcement and COVID-19. Baseline: 0 Target: 3,000

The project leveraged UN local and international resources from Ministry of Justice, Human Rights Commission UN Police, and the Office of the High Commissioner on Human Rights to support the response efforts of the Zambia Police Service.
Financial and technical resources enabled the Zambia Police Service to develop comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures to guide law enforcement response to COVID-19. Through virtual training, the UN enhanced the skills of police officers in international policing and human rights standards as well as general information about COVID-19.
Support enabled the development of training guidelines and tools for the master trainers. The Zambia Police Service Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) Against COVID-19 include strong human rights and gender dimensions and provide for various scenarios depending on the gravity of the COVID-19 cases and prevention measures announced by government.
The SOPs will enable the Zambia Police Service which includes over 22,000 officers to act appropriately in enforcing COVID-19 measures.
